item.title: Anthropic vs OpenAI: How Claude maker’s growth is challenging ChatGPT ahead of IPO
item.description: Anthropic has seen significant revenue growth, reaching $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026. OpenAI continues to expand its business model while generating substantial revenues from its consumer and enterprise offerings. Both companies face financial pressures as they invest heavily in infrastructure and computing power. The competition between Anthropic and OpenAI is primarily driven by their customer acquisition strategies and operational efficiencies.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has emerged as a strong challenger to OpenAI in the race to sell artificial intelligence to businesses, with its revenue rising sharply as demand for its Claude models grows. But investors weighing the two companies must look beyond sales growth to understand which business is better placed to deliver returns.Anthropic, which unveiled its initial public offering filing on Monday, reported revenue of $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026. OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reported quarterly revenue of $6.7 billion in the second quarter, according to Reuters.The figures suggest Anthropic has built strong momentum in the enterprise market, where companies pay to use AI for software development, data analysis and other business tasks. But the comparison is not straightforward because the two companies account for some sales through cloud partners differently.OpenAI has also been expanding rapidly and remains a major player in the consumer AI market. The competition between the two companies is therefore likely to depend on their ability to attract paying customers, control computing costs and turn revenue growth into cash.Revenue growth favours AnthropicAnthropic’s revenue rose to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million in 2024, according to its IPO filing. Revenue for the first six months of 2026 reached $16.29 billion.The company has benefited from growing demand for Claude, particularly its coding tools, which help software developers write, check and fix code. Its products are also used by businesses seeking to automate work and build AI-powered applications.OpenAI, meanwhile, has expanded beyond ChatGPT into business software, developer tools and AI agents. Reuters reported in October that OpenAI’s annualised revenue run rate for September was close to $50 billion, lower than the nearly $70 billion figure it had previously indicated to investors.An annualised revenue run rate estimates a full year’s revenue by extending a recent period’s sales. It is not the same as revenue actually earned over a year.Also Read: Anthropic IPO: 5 jaw-dropping numbers investors need to know about $1.5 trillion public offerIt should be noted that Anthropic records the full value of certain sales made through cloud marketplaces as revenue and records the platform fees separately. OpenAI does not include some similar cloud-partner sales in its revenue figures.This difference makes it difficult to determine which company has the larger underlying business from headline revenue alone.The profitability questionRapid revenue growth has not removed the financial risks facing either company.Anthropic reported an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, according to its IPO filing. Its reported net loss was much larger, at $80.7 billion, largely because of a non-cash accounting charge linked to the increased estimated value of bonds that may eventually convert into company shares.The operating loss provides a better indication of the gap between the company’s operating income and expenses during the period, although it does not by itself show how much cash the company generated or used.OpenAI also faces heavy spending requirements. Reuters reported in September, citing a Financial Times report, that the company expected to use about $278 billion in cash between 2026 and 2030 as it invests in computing power and infrastructure.The figures are not directly comparable because they cover different periods and measures. However, they underline the challenge facing both companies: advanced AI requires large investments in computing capacity, data centres, chips and research before the companies can generate sustainable returns.Computing costs and Big Tech dependenceAnthropic depends heavily on Amazon and Google for computing infrastructure and access to business customers. Both companies are also investors in Anthropic and compete with it in AI.Reuters reported that Amazon and Google’s cloud marketplaces accounted for 47% of Anthropic’s sales to customers in 2025. These relationships help Claude reach businesses already using their cloud services, but they also expose Anthropic to dependence on a small number of powerful partners.OpenAI has its own infrastructure requirements and strategic partnerships, including its close relationship with Microsoft. It has also been committing substantial sums to secure computing capacity for future AI development.The companies’ ability to manage these commitments will be important as competition increases. If AI usage grows more slowly than expected, large infrastructure obligations could weigh on cash flow. If demand continues to rise rapidly, access to computing power could become a competitive advantage.Also Read : Anthropic IPO: What should investors consider when valuing the AI company? Aswath Damodaran explainsValuation will determine investor returnsBoth companies are seeking valuations that reflect expectations of enormous future growth.Anthropic has been valued by some investors at around $1.5 trillion in recent discussions, below expectations of about $2 trillion reported earlier. OpenAI has also been linked to a potential valuation exceeding $1.4 trillion in recent fundraising talks, according to Reuters.These are reported private-market valuations and fundraising discussions, not necessarily the final prices at which either company’s shares will be offered to public investorA higher valuation does not automatically mean a company is better placed. Investors must assess how much future growth is already reflected in the price and whether the company can deliver the revenue and profits needed to justify it.Anthropic’s upcoming IPO could provide a useful benchmark for valuing AI businesses. OpenAI’s eventual listing, expected later, could give investors another opportunity to compare the companies using more detailed financial disclosures.Which business is better placed?Anthropic currently has a strong case based on its rapid revenue growth and position in business AI, particularly coding. Its latest disclosures also give investors a clearer view of its operating performance and infrastructure commitments.OpenAI has a broad consumer presence through ChatGPT, a growing enterprise business and significant financial and technology partnerships. Its scale gives it opportunities to sell AI products across a wide range of users and applications.

item.title: Anthropic IPO: Rising costs, risks, rapid growth mark AI frontrunner
item.description: Anthropic, established by ex OpenAI researchers, is gearing up for an anticipated entry into the stock market in the United States. The organization has impressively generated $16.29 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026. Yet, significant operational losses due to soaring computing costs pose a challenge, along with over $500 billion in cloud computing commitments. Competing against OpenAI and Google, they must adeptly maneuver through a tough economic environment.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Anthropic’s US IPO filing puts a fresh spotlight on the high cost of staying ahead in artificial intelligence, with the Claude maker showing explosive revenue growth while taking on enormous spending commitments and widening losses, according to Reuters.The company unveiled its IPO paperwork on Monday after confidentially filing in June.Revenue surges, but losses remain steepFounded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic has built a strong position in the AI race through its Claude models, particularly in coding and enterprise applications.The company's revenue surged to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million in 2024 and $41 million in 2023. It then more than tripled to $16.29 billion in the first six months of 2026. But the rapid expansion is proving expensive. Anthropic recorded an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, after losing $8.06 billion in 2025, compared with $2.98 billion a year earlier, Reuters reported.Compute race comes with billion dollar commitmentsComputing power is at the heart of Anthropic’s cost structure, with the company spending on cloud services, data centres, equipment leases and energy.It has committed more than $500 billion with six partners over a decade, including at least $110 billion with Amazon, about $114.5 billion with Google and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years.That spending also reflects the increasingly interconnected nature of AI financing. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic’s biggest backers. Amazon has invested at least $13 billion and agreed to invest up to another $20 billion, while Google has committed up to $40 billion.Anthropic will retain a governance structure that gives its founders significant control after the listing. As a public benefit corporation, it is also required to balance investor interests with its broader mission of developing AI for the benefit of humanity.Competition is intensifying as OpenAI, Google and Elon Musk’s SpaceX pour billions into models, data centres and specialised chips. Ramp data showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1% of AI token spending in the week ended October 11, highlighting the momentum behind Claude as the IPO brings its spending model under greater investor scrutiny, Reuters reported.

item.title: Anthropic's top investors include Amazon, Google, Fidelity Management
item.description: Anthropic is preparing for its initial public offering, supported by significant investments from Amazon and Google. The company's valuation has increased significantly through numerous funding rounds over recent periods. Key investors like ICONIQ Capital and Coatue Management have also expressed confidence in its potential. Anthropic's partnerships with technology leaders enhance its resources for advancing AI development.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is gearing up for its initial public offering, showcasing robust support from heavyweight investors like Amazon and Google. The company’s valuation has surged through various funding rounds, signaling considerable confidence from the investment community. Collaborations with technology leaders provide vital resources essential for advancing AI development and infrastructure. Notable financial participants include ICONIQ Capital, Coatue Management, and Eric Schmidt, among several others.Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds. Its initial public offering now offers a closely watched test of whether investors beyond Silicon Valley share that enthusiasm for the leaders of the AI boom.Here's a look at the key investors backing the Claude maker: Amazon Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and in April agreed to invest up to an additional $20 billion. Anthropic also committed to spend more than $100 billion on the e-commerce giant's cloud services over 10 years.Alphabet's Google Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic, including an initial $10 billion investment announced in April.The partnership provides Anthropic with cloud infrastructure and access to Google's AI chips, which are used to train and run Claude models.Spark Capital Spark Capital led Anthropic's $450 million Series C round in May 2023 and gained board representation through general partner Yasmin Razavi.Lightspeed Venture Lightspeed led the $3.5 billion Series Partners E round in March 2025 and later co-led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation in September that year.Fidelity Management Fidelity participated in Series E and & Research co-led the $13 billion Series F financing at a $183 billion valuation.The firm's other investments include Databricks and CoreWeave.Salesforce Ventures Salesforce Ventures participated in the $450 million Series C round and the $3.5 billion Series E financing. The software firm's venture arm has also invested in firms such as Cohere and Chainguard.ICONIQ Capital ICONIQ led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation and later co-led the $30 billion Series G financing.The venture capital firm's investments include OpenAI and smart ring maker Oura.GIC SingaporeGIC Singapore's sovereign wealth fund led the $30 billion Series G round at a $380 billion valuation. GIC has also invested in AI voice generation startup ElevenLabs.Coatue Management Coatue led the $30 billion Series G financing and later co-led the $65 billion Series H round.The investment firm has also financed companies such as Canva and CoreWeave.D1 Capital Partners D1 Capital invested across multiple large financings including Series E, Series F, Series G and Series H. The firm has holdings in Cognition AI and SpaceX.Sequoia Capital Sequoia was a significant investor in Series G and became one of the lead investors in the $65 billion Series H round at a $965 billion valuation. Altimeter Capital Altimeter invested in the September 2025 $13 billion fundraise and was a lead investor in the $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion valuation.Jaan Tallinn Skype co-founder Tallinn led Anthropic's first institutional financing, a $124 million Series A round in 2021.The angel investor has also funded open-source AI startup Zyphra and Rain AI.Eric Schmidt The former Google chief executive has backed Anthropic personally and is among the company's best-known individual investors. Schmidt has also funded Yann LeCun's Advanced Machine Intelligence Menlo Ventures Menlo participated in major late-stage financings, including the $3.5 billion Series E round at a $61.5 billion valuation.

item.title: US stocks today: US stocks rise as Anthropic IPO puts AI spending under scrutiny
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes experienced gains as technology stocks led the rise amid AI investment discussions. Investors are preparing for a busy week of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rates. Anthropic's IPO filing highlights both the demand for AI and associated development costs, creating investor caution. Chip stocks, benefiting from the AI boom, showed strong performance overall.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's main indexes rose on Monday as investors weighed Anthropic's plans for a US listing against growing questions over whether massive AI investments can deliver sustainable returns. Technology stocks led the gains, while investors also looked ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, Reuters reported.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.45%, the S&P 500 gained 0.57% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.46% in early trading.Anthropic filing puts AI spending back in focusAnthropic disclosed steep losses alongside rapid revenue growth in its IPO filing, highlighting both the scale of demand for AI and the heavy costs involved in developing the technology, according to Reuters.The filing comes as investors are becoming more selective about AI spending. About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. Their results are expected to provide clues on whether large investments in AI are translating into stronger growth, Reuters reported. It's a challenging environment, to say the least exactly when this IPO will take place, but there's a lot riding on not only the company, but the AI industry, said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield.The concerns have already weighed on some AI linked companies. Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius fell after Elon Musk said markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, and predicted consolidation in the sector, Reuters reported.Tesla jumps while Fed decision loomsChip stocks, among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, were among the strongest performers, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index rising about 1%, Reuters reported.Tesla gained 5.9% to a more than three month high after Barclays upgraded the stock to overweight from equal weight .Investors are also positioning for the Fed's policy decision on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected following its September rate hike. Attention will then turn to September's Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation data and third quarter GDP, both due Thursday, according to Reuters.Crude oil prices eased after reaching a near six month high last week, while investors continued to monitor efforts to de escalate regional tensions.
